cars.generation: Fourth-generation BL/BP Legacy production-road sporting family
cars.specification_market: Fourth-generation Legacy / Liberty sporting-road family, selected 2005 Canadian Legacy 2.5GT Limited sedan with five-speed manual, from Subaru Canada brochure SBL05E printed in Canada in 2004. One family across BL/BP sedan/wagon, B4/Liberty regional names, engines, Spec.B, STI derivatives, years and related fourth-generation Outback versions; no extra body/trim record. Existing BC/BF and BE/BH S401 are earlier generations. All technical fields use the Canadian reference, not US tests or Japanese 2.0-litre figures. Nominal 2.5 litres only: no exact cc, engine-code suffix, Japanese twin-scroll system, claimed 100-kg reduction, US measured performance or aftermarket suspension imported. Manual viscous centre differential is separate from automatic VTD; curb mass is the manual Limited sedan column, not wagon or automatic.
cars.summary: The fourth-generation Legacy GT brought WRX-like turbo performance to an understated all-weather grand tourer. Contemporary testing records its sleeper appeal and practical character alongside chassis and ownership limitations. Bodies, markets and variants remain one family.

sources.notes: Downloaded 24-spread PDF. Cover/back-cover spread index 0 and final spreads indices 22–23 individually inspected as rendered images; printed pp. 44–45 contain selected technical and equipment tables. All 20 attributes map to this Canadian source. Cover identifies subaru.ca and Canadian publication; filename alone did not establish market. Other rendered spreads are not claimed as visually reviewed. No complete 48-page visual audit, exact engine cc/code, US figures, automatic VTD or Japanese twin-scroll technology inferred.

sources.title: Legacy awarded Car of the Year Japan 2003–2004 — 13 November 2003
sources.source_type: Original manufacturer award and generation account
sources.notes: Complete relevant release read. Subaru’s first Japan Car of the Year award applies to the new Legacy range, not certification of this Canadian GT Limited specification or a motorsport victory. The release describes a new engine/chassis/body programme and its grand-touring purpose; no numerical technical value imported.

sources.title: 2005 Subaru Legacy 2.5GT Limited — Dave VanderWerp, 1 August 2006 long-term test
sources.notes: Relevant complete body read, including stock-car limitations and separate aftermarket section. Admission context only; no technical values or modified-car results imported. Individual-car faults, optional short shifter, driver misfuelling and dealer installation damage are distinguished, not presented as universal production defects.

sources.title: Sports Sedan Comparo — Patrick Bedard, October 2004 issue, Legacy GT section
sources.notes: Introduction and complete Legacy section/panel read. Third-place overall finish and chassis limits retained; no class-winner claim. Article’s displayed 2004 test-car label does not define the Canadian 2005 reference. No US measured figure, mass, boost pressure or optional equipment imported.

facts.title: A milestone for the Legacy generation
facts.explanation: The new Legacy range received the 2003–2004 Car of the Year Japan award, Subaru’s first such win. This recognises the generation rather than certifying an individual Canadian GT specification.
